problem: Prior emergent-communication work uses simplified reference games or 2D grid worlds. Work in 3D embodied settings only asks whether communication improves task success, so there is no systematic interpretation of what heterogeneous embodied agents actually communicate or whether it is grounded in perception.
motivation: Real-world collaboration often pairs agents with different capabilities and information, such as a phone guide and a driver. Understanding whether learned messages are interpretable and grounded in egocentric perception and 3D spatial structure is needed to study grounded communication for embodied navigation.
key_idea: Introduce CoMON, a collaborative multi-object navigation task in which a map-holding oracle talks to a visually navigating agent. Use it to compare unstructured (continuous vector) and structured (soft discrete vocabulary) communication, and interpret the messages with probes and classifiers in an egocentric, spatial frame.
insight: Imposing a message structure (a softmax over a small learned vocabulary) yields more efficient and better-generalizing communication than free real-valued vectors. In 3-ON, S-Comm PPL is 50 vs 39 for U-Comm; on 5-ON, Progress is 52 vs 26 (Table 4 lists 35 vs 26 for 5-ON). Random-message baselines fall back to NoCom-level performance, showing the learned messages carry real information. Probes and classifiers show the messages encode the goal color (navigator to oracle) and the goal's egocentric direction and distance (oracle to navigator). Symbol-conditioned action statistics show positive listening. When the goal is visible, the navigator ignores the oracle and relies on perception.
method: CoMON task: extends multiON. A disembodied oracle A_O sees a top-down semantic map (occupancy plus goal objects) and A_N's pose. A navigator A_N sees RGBD and the current goal category, and must find an ordered sequence of goals using FORWARD/LEFT/RIGHT/FOUND.

Unstructured communication (U-Comm): the belief is passed through a linear layer to a real-valued message. The receiver concatenates the message with its belief, applies two FC layers and a skip connection to refine the belief. There are two communication rounds per step.

Structured communication (S-Comm): the belief goes through a linear layer and softmax to give probabilities over K learned word embeddings. The receiver decodes the message as the probability-weighted sum of embeddings, then refines its belief as in U-Comm. Gumbel-Softmax discrete tokens failed to train.

Architecture: TBONE-style. The oracle crops and rotates the map into an egocentric 45x45 map, encoded by a CNN. The navigator encodes RGBD with a CNN. Beliefs are refined by communication, then a GRU, then actor and critic heads. Trained with PPO under centralized training and decentralized execution, using the navigator reward (goal +3, geodesic progress, -0.01 time penalty).

Interpretation framework: linear probes (U-Comm) and random forests (S-Comm) relate messages to goal color and egocentric goal position or angle. Symbols are binned by probability thresholds. Positive signaling and positive listening are checked via action distributions per symbol.
Baselines: NoCom, Rand U-Comm, Rand S-Comm (lower bounds), and OracleMap (a single agent with the map, upper bound).

setting.backbone: TBONE-style CNN + GRU actor-critic agents (oracle map encoder and navigator RGBD encoder), trained from scratch with PPO
setting.training_data: multiON dataset on Matterport3D scenes (50,000 episodes per scene for train), trained on 3-ON for 50M steps
setting.observation: Navigator: egocentric RGBD, goal category one-hot, previous action. Oracle: top-down 300x300 semantic occupancy/goal map plus navigator pose.
setting.action_space: Low-level discrete: FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN LEFT/RIGHT 30°, FOUND, plus two rounds of inter-agent messages per step
setting.privileged: The oracle agent has a GT top-down semantic map with goal positions and the navigator's GT pose, by task design. The navigator has no privileged information.

numbers.extra: trained on 3-ON for 50M steps; message length 2
numbers.evidence: Table 1 (Progress 70, PPL 50 for 3-ON) and Table 4 (Success 58, SPL 45)

numbers.eval_set_note: 1,000 validation episodes; generalization to 5-ON, trained on 3-ON

numbers_note: Main text says '5-ON (S-Comm PROGRESS is 52% vs. U-Comm 26%)' but Table 4 gives 35 (S-Comm) and 26 (U-Comm), an inconsistency in the paper. S-Comm on 1-ON and 2-ON: Progress 85 and 80, PPL 67 and 59. Also 4-ON: S-Comm Progress 50 (main text says 63 vs 41 for U-Comm; Table 4 lists 50 vs 41).
results: Random-message baselines stay near NoCom (3-ON Progress 26 to 28), while U-Comm (63) and S-Comm (70) approach OracleMap (70). S-Comm is more efficient than U-Comm (PPL 50 vs 39 on 3-ON) and generalizes better to 4-ON and 5-ON.
limitations: The oracle is given the navigator's exact position and orientation. Hiding it made learning fail, so localization is factored out.
The setting is restricted to simple synthetic cylinder goals in multiON, and the interpretation is correlational (probes and classifiers) with modest accuracies (e.g. 58% and 69.7%).
Discrete Gumbel-Softmax messages could not be trained, so 'structured' communication is a soft, differentiable vocabulary, and bandwidth is small (2 words or 2 dims).
